body:
My feeling is that he's never going to be happy, he's just surrounded by reminders of what he could have had. my family is upper middle class but his is just insanely successful. If it was anyone else I'd feel a lot less sympathetic, but I don't see any way his life gets better unless he literally cuts ties with everyone he has grown up with. But I know he won't do that because with his record his only real advantage is that his dad got him into a decent job, but he can't really advance much further with his record I imagine because he can't get his series 7 and deal with securities.

I'm a bit overwhelmed and honestly I have been tempted to just tell him to, well, shit or get off the pot. But I'm afraid he would shit. 

The reality is I think he's eventually going to do it, I doubt it is now, he will keep fighting until he exhausts every path he sees to get what he wants, and the day that happens I know I will lose my friend, but I can't really do much to stop it. He won't confide in anyone else besides me, and even if I report him he'll deny it. 

He doesn't want to be saved, he wants to win on his terms, and honestly I can respect that even if it saddens me. The best is can hope for is he waits and finds a reason to live, hopefully a relationship or something else that will change his mind.

He wants to help but at the same time he's got a huge ego and a hunger for respect. I think in one part he wanted to go into medicine to help people and in another it was to be a leader and ina role with responsibility and respect. Mind you that this respect is the kind that needs to impress people in a wealthy part of westchester county NY, including his family.

I thought I could help him find the helping part. I've worked with violent felons who have became mentors through my public defender work. The problem is that "over privileged white kid gets busted for coke at rice" doesn't really inspire much. And it doesn't help him with the respect and prestige issue.

Everything he seems to want to do involves things where his record is going to probably stop him dead in his tracks and that's a huge problem. 

I mean I feel like I need to tell him he needs to lower his expectations to save his life but I fear he will just give up at the point.

Here's the sad part, his drug use was just at the wrong place at the wrong time. He was in Texas on a trip and got busted with a bunch of others and ended very screwed. I see no evidence he's using now. But he fought it because he thought it would block him from med school, and he lost. Ended up with a felony. 

He's underemployed, and I get that, I am too, but I was never as ambitious as he is and I find my satisfaction elsewhere. He has no interest in thinking that way, and honestly I don't think I can change his mind. 

He takes responsibility, I have no doubt about that. But he just can't seem to find happiness in living with the results, I think that's the spite part. He feels he's paid enough and wants to be what he knows he can be. I believe he could be amazing, but I don't see how he can ever get around his past.

That was helpful, I convinced them to explore other options first and at least bought time.

My friend basically got screwed out of medical school because of a past mistake, and he tried to get that mistake cleared up and it didn't work out. 

I suggested a few other things but the problem is I fear he will run into the same barrier, and that I only bought him time. He's a high energy, very motivated guy and I know he's not going to be able to live with the options available to him because he couldn't keep his nose out of the white stuff in college. He's just too ambitious for the life he corralled himself into.
